method: Two research helpers read official code sites where they could; many state sites and Justia refused the requests, so entries below 'high' come from the helpers' recall of the statute and are unverified. The game treats every non-high entry as an estimate (stopgap SG-WORLD-housing-eviction-steps). A second pass (Oct 12) read official code sites with curl; records it confirmed carry verifiedFields and a quote. Third pass (Oct 12, 2026): hearing and stay periods read from official text for 40 places (hearingStaySources).
fields: noticeDays (pay-or-quit), cureAllowed, gracePeriodDays, answerOrHearingDays, appealOrStayDays, removalBy, statute, sourceUrl, confidence, note

US-NC.note: Read 42-3 and 42-26/42-29. 42-3 implies forfeiture if rent unpaid 10 days after demand in leases with a fixed rent date (practice: landlords serve a 10-day demand; treat as 10 calendar days if the lease has no other rule). Original null left because the 42-26 ground does not itself require the demand. 42-29 summons service text read; 5-day late-fee grace (42-46) text was not confirmed in retrieved output.

Removal delay is the 10-day appeal window; 42-36.2 also requires 2 days' (5 by mail) notice before the sheriff executes the writ.

US-NJ.note: Read in official NJ statutes text file. No pre-suit notice for nonpayment (2A:18-61.2 exempts it). Warrant executed not earlier than the 3rd day after personal service, excluding weekends/court holidays (2A:42-10.16(b)), so appealOrStayDays 3 is business days. Hearing window not verified.
US-NJ.quote: 2A:18-61.2: "No judgment of possession shall be entered ... except in the nonpayment of rent under subsection a. or f. of section 2, unless the landlord has made written demand and given written notice"

US-NV.note: CORRECTION: current NRS 40.253(1)(a) is 7 judicial days, not 10. Weekly tenancies of 45 days or less may use noon of the 4th full day. After the order, sheriff/constable posts within 24 hours and removes not earlier than 24 nor later than 36 hours after posting. Appeal within 10 judicial days of the order (NRS 40.385); the tenant affidavit is due by the notice deadline, so answerOrHearingDays 10 is unverified and probably 7 judicial days. Left as original; owner to review.

hearingStaySources.note: In Nevada's summary eviction the tenant's answer (affidavit) is due by the end of the 7-judicial-day notice period; the statute sets no separate hearing deadline. File value [10,10] is not supported. Did not re-verify appealOrStayDays (already verified in file as 10); removal itself is 24-36 hours after posting of the order.

RPAPL 749(2)(a): "The officer to whom the warrant is directed and delivered shall give at least fourteen days' notice, in writing"
hearingStaySources.note: Read via WebFetch (nysenate.gov returns 403 to curl). For nonpayment, RPAPL 732 governs: answer within 10 days of service, trial 3-8 days after joinder. The file's [10,17] comes from RPAPL 733(1), which expressly excludes nonpayment proceedings ('Except as provided in section seven hundred thirty-two ... relating to a proceeding for non-payment of rent'). Whether a local court rule displaces 732 was not checked.

US-OH.note: Read 1923.04(A). 3 or more days notice to leave. Cure not verified.
US-OH.quote: ORC 1923.04(A): party "shall notify the adverse party to leave the premises ... three or more days before beginning the action, by certified mail ... or by handing a written copy of the notice"

quotes: 1923.06(A): "Such service shall be at least seven days before the day set for trial."

1923.14(A): "...within ten days after receiving a writ of execution ... the sheriff, police officer, constable, or bailiff shall execute it by restoring the plaintiff to the possession of the premises"
hearingStaySources.note: Current text requires service at least 7 days before trial (file has 5); no statutory maximum found. No statutory waiting period before the writ issues; 1923.14 gives the officer up to 10 days after receipt to execute it, which is an outer limit, not a stay (file's 10 likely reflects this).

US-OK.note: Read official Title 41 text. Payment within 5 days after written demand avoids termination; demand for rent is deemed a demand for possession. Title 12 timing fields not verified.
US-OK.quote: 41 O.S. 131(B): "A landlord may terminate a rental agreement for failure to pay rent when due, if the tenant fails to pay the rent within five (5) days after written notice of landlord's demand for payment."

quotes: 1148.4: "...summon the defendant to appear for trial at the time and place specified therein, which time shall be not less than five (5) days nor more than ten (10) days from the date that the summons is issued."
1148.5: "...such service shall be at least three (3) days before the day of trial"
1148.10A(A): "...the plaintiff or agent of the plaintiff or officer shall return in forty-eight (48) hours to restore the plaintiff possession of the premises by executing the writ"
hearingStaySources.note: Writ issues on request after judgment (no waiting period); tenant gets 48 hours' notice before execution (recorded as 2). A new-trial motion within 3 days does not stay execution. File's 10-day stay is not supported.

US-OR.note: CORRECTION: current ORS 90.394 (amended 2023 c.13, c.296) is 10 days written notice, given no sooner than the 8th day of the rental period (so 7 days of grace); alternative 13-day notice may be given from the 5th day. Week-to-week tenancies: 72 hours, from the 5th day. Notice must state amount and date/time to cure, so cure by payment is allowed. Hearing/appeal fields not verified.
US-OR.quote: 90.394(2)(a): "At least 10 days written notice of nonpayment and the landlord's intention to terminate the rental agreement if the rent is not paid within that period ... no sooner than on the eighth day of the rental period"

quotes: 105.135(2)(a): "The clerk shall calculate the first appearance, which shall be: (A) Seven days after the judicial day next following payment of the filing fees; or (B) If the claim for possession is brought under ORS 90.392 or 90.394 for nonpayment ... 15 days after the judicial day next following payment of the filing fees."
105.135(2)(b): "The clerk may delay the first appearance by up to seven days"
105.151(1)(a): "...a notice of restitution that shall give the defendant four days to move out of the premises"
hearingStaySources.note: For nonpayment, first appearance is 15 days after the judicial day following filing-fee payment (service happens by the end of that next judicial day), extendable by up to 7 days (so 15-22). The 7-day figure in the file's [7,15] applies only to non-rent claims. Stay: 4-day notice of restitution before the writ.

US-PA.note: Read official PA text. 10-day notice to quit for nonpayment. Summons date is 7-10 days from summons (502(a)). Writ of possession issues after the 5th day after judgment, served within 48 hours and executed on the 11th day after service (503(b)). Tenant can supersede the writ by paying arrears and costs any time before execution (503(c)). Appeal within 10 days of judgment (513(b)); supersedeas only if tenant pays judgment in cash/bond.
US-PA.quote: 250.501(b): "In case of failure of the tenant, upon demand, to satisfy any rent reserved and due, the notice shall specify that the tenant shall remove within ten days from the date of the service thereof."

US-PR.statute: 32 L.P.R.A. 2821 et seq. (Codigo de Enjuiciamiento Civil Arts. 620-634; Ley 140-1974)
US-PR.note: Could not retrieve text; summary desahucio court proceeding; details unresolved.
US-PR.verificationFailed: Not attempted beyond reachability checks; no Puerto Rico statute host tried successfully.

hearingStaySources.statute: Codigo de Enjuiciamiento Civil Art. 623 (32 LPRA sec. 2824), Art. 625 (32 LPRA sec. 2826), Art. 629 (32 LPRA sec. 2831 per the court's footnote)
quotes: Art. 623 as quoted by the PR Court of Appeals (KLAN202400725): "...se mandará a convocar al actor y al demandado para comparecencia, que deberá celebrarse dentro de los diez (10) días siguientes a aquel en que se presente la reclamación"

Art. 629 as quoted in KLAN202300640 (poderjudicial.pr): "Las apelaciones deberán interponerse en el término de cinco (5) días, contados desde la fecha de archivo en autos de la notificación de la sentencia"
hearingStaySources.note: Statute text read as quoted verbatim in official Puerto Rico Judicial Branch (Court of Appeals) decisions, not from the OGP code PDF directly. Hearing within 10 days of filing (no minimum stated); judgment within 10 days after evidence closes (Art. 625); appeal window 5 days from notice of judgment. Lanzamiento (removal) timing after the appeal window not checked.

US-RI.note: Read 34-18-35. Notice only after rent is 15 days in arrears; tenant cures by paying within 5 days of mailing; action filed no earlier than the 6th day after mailing.
US-RI.quote: 34-18-35(a): rent "in arrears for fifteen (15) days, the landlord shall send a written notice ... unless he or she cures the breach within five (5) days of the date of mailing of the notice, the rental agreement shall terminate"

quotes: 34-18-35(c): "The summons for eviction for nonpayment of rent shall specify the date for hearing and be in the form provided in § 34-18-56(g). The summons shall specify that the defendant may file and serve his or her answer prior to or at the time of hearing"
9-12-10.1: "...by claiming an appeal from the judgment ... in writing, filed with the clerk of the division within five (5) days after the judgment is entered"
hearingStaySources.note: Statute leaves the nonpayment hearing date to the summons; no service-to-hearing day count found in 34-18-35 or the 34-18-56 forms (likely set by District Court rule, not checked). Appeal window 5 days.

US-SC.note: Read § 27-40-710(B): the tenant has five days from the due date to pay; the written notice may be a conspicuous lease clause. Hearing and stay periods (title 27, chapter 37) not yet read.

quotes: 27-37-20: "...issue a written rule requiring the tenant forthwith to vacate the premises occupied by him or to show cause why he should not be ejected before the magistrate within ten days after service of a copy of such rule upon the tenant."
27-37-100: "If the verdict be for the plaintiff the magistrate shall within five days issue a writ of ejectment"
27-37-160: "...present to the occupants a copy of the writ and give the occupants twenty-four hours to vacate voluntarily."
hearingStaySources.note: The 10-day show-cause period is in chapter 37 (Ejectment), not 27-40-710. The 5 days in 27-37-100 is an outer limit for the magistrate to issue the writ, not a mandatory wait; the tenant's guaranteed period after the writ is 24 hours (recorded as 1). File value 5 is defensible only as the writ-issuance outer limit.

US-SD.note: Read SD codified law. CORRECTION: SDCL 21-16-2 was repealed (SL 2024 ch 75). Nonpayment ground is 3 days after rent is due (21-16-1(4)), with no separate written notice found. Appearance and pleading due 5 days from service (21-16-7); trial on 2 days notice after issue joined (21-16-8); adjournments capped at 14 days without bond. Cure not addressed.
US-SD.quote: 21-16-1(4): action maintainable "If a lessee in person or by subtenants holds over ... or fails to pay his rent for three days after the same shall be due"

quotes: 21-16-7: "The time for appearance and pleading shall be five days from the time of service on the defendant or thirty days after the publication of service under § 21-16-6.1, whichever occurs sooner."
hearingStaySources.note: Amended SL 2024 ch 75. Stay of execution not checked.

US-TN.note: URLTA counties: rent 5 days late, then 14-day notice to cure; non-URLTA counties use common law demand; detainer warrant return 3-6 days; 10 days to appeal.
US-TN.verificationFailed: wapp.capitol.tn.gov code pages are a JavaScript app (no text via curl); Justia returns 403.

US-TX.note: Read statute: 3-day notice unless lease says otherwise; trial 10-21 days after filing and not before 4th day after service; writ not before 6th day after judgment, 24-hour posted warning.

quotes: 24.0051(g): "(1) shall ... hold the trial of an eviction suit on a date that is not earlier than the 10th day or later than the 21st day after the date the petition is filed; (2) may not hold the trial on a date that is earlier than the fourth day after the date the tenant is served"
24.005107(a): "...not later than the fifth day after the date the judgment is signed."
24.0061(b): "A writ of possession may not be issued before the sixth day after the date on which the judgment for possession is rendered unless a possession bond has been filed"
hearingStaySources.note: Post-2025 text. 10-21 is from filing; trial also at least 4 days after service; summary disposition response due by 4th day after service. Writ may issue on the 6th day (5-day appeal window); then a 24-hour posted warning before execution (24.0061(d)).

US-UT.note: Recalled, not read; 3 business days notice; answer 3 business days after service; hearing within 10 days of request.
US-UT.verificationFailed: le.utah.gov connection fails through the proxy (no response).

US-VA.note: CORRECTION: current (effective-until-July 1, 2027) text of 55.1-1245(F) says 14 days, not 5 (page read 2026-10-12, amended by 2025 cc.684/688 and 2026 cc.353/354/844). Paying within 14 days avoids termination. 55.1-1250 governs redemption/acceptance of rent. Hearing, appeal and grace fields not verified.
US-VA.quote: 55.1-1245(F): "If rent is unpaid when due, and the tenant fails to pay rent within 14 days after written notice is served on him ... the landlord may terminate the rental agreement"

quotes: 8.01-126: "...the initial hearing on such summons shall occur as soon as practicable, but not more than 21 days from the date of filing." ... "Such summons shall be served at least 10 days before the return day thereof."
8.01-129: "The appeal shall be taken within 10 days and the security approved by the court from which the appeal is taken."
8.01-470: "...the officer to whom a writ of eviction has been delivered to be executed shall, at least 72 hours before execution, serve notice of intent to execute"
hearingStaySources.note: Min 10 = service before return day; max 21 from filing (up to 30 if court cannot hear sooner). Removal delay: 10-day appeal window plus 72-hour notice of execution.

US-VI.note: Recalled 3-day notice from statute language; a secondary source said 14 days; unresolved.
US-VI.verificationFailed: legvi.org/www.legvi.org vicode returns 404/522; vilegislature.org blocked by proxy.

US-VT.note: Read 4467(a). Cure by paying rent due through the end of the rental period in which payment is made. Hearing/writ fields not verified.
US-VT.quote: 9 V.S.A. 4467(a): termination date "shall be at least 14 days after the date of the actual notice. The rental agreement shall not terminate if the tenant pays or tenders rent due through the end of the rental period"

quotes: 4854: "The writ shall direct any sheriff to serve the writ upon the defendant and, not earlier than 14 days after the writ is served, to put the plaintiff into possession."
4853a(b): "A hearing on the motion shall be held any time after 14 days' notice to the parties."
hearingStaySources.note: 12 V.S.A. ch. 169 sets no answer period; the answer deadline comes from the general civil rules (V.R.C.P. 12(a), not checked here). 4853a(b) is the rent-escrow motion hearing (14 days' notice), not the merits hearing.

US-WA.note: Read RCW 59.12.030(3) and 59.18.057. Notice is pay-or-vacate in the alternative, 14 days after service. Other fields (hearing, writ) not verified.
US-WA.quote: RCW 59.12.030(3): notice "requiring in the alternative the payment of the rent or the surrender of the detained premises ... for the period of 14 days after service for tenancies under chapter 59.18 RCW."

quotes: 59.18.370: "...fix a time and place for a hearing of the motion, which shall not be less than seven nor more than thirty days from the date of service of the order upon defendant."

59.18.410(2): "When the tenant is liable for unlawful detainer after a default in the payment of rent, execution upon the judgment shall not occur until the expiration of five court days after the entry of the judgment."
59.18.390(1): "The sheriff shall, upon receiving the writ of restitution, forthwith serve a copy thereof upon the tenant ... and shall not execute the same for three days thereafter."
hearingStaySources.note: Show-cause hearing window. Stay is 5 court days (nonpayment), and the sheriff must also wait 3 days after serving the writ.

US-WI.note: Read 704.17(2)(a). 5 days for leases of one year or less and year-to-year tenancies; if tenant already received a pay-or-vacate notice, paid, and defaults again within one year, landlord may give 14-day notice to vacate (no cure). Longer leases use 704.17(1) (not read).
US-WI.quote: 704.17(2)(a): tenant who "fails to pay any installment of rent when due, the tenant's tenancy is terminated if the landlord gives the tenant notice requiring the tenant to pay rent or vacate on or before a date at least 5 days after the giving of the notice"

quotes: 799.05(3)(b): "In eviction actions, the return date for a summons served upon a resident of this state shall be not less than 5 days nor more than 25 days from the issue date, and service shall be made not less than 5 days prior to the return date."
799.44(2): "At the time of ordering judgment for the restitution of premises, the court shall immediately order that a writ of restitution be issued"
799.44(3): "...the court may, in cases where it determines hardship to exist, stay the issuance of the writ by a period not to exceed 30 days"
hearingStaySources.note: Writ issues immediately (0); hardship stay up to 30 days is discretionary; 15-day appeal (799.445) stays only with an undertaking. Chapter PDF current through Oct 1, 2026.

US-WV.note: Read 55-3A-1. No pre-suit notice appears in the petition requirement; hearing 5-10 judicial days after filing (answerOrHearingDays is in judicial days); written defense due within 5 days of receipt of hearing notice. Notice and cure for nonpayment still unconfirmed.
US-WV.quote: 55-3A-1(b): "the court shall schedule a hearing, which may not be less than five nor more than 10 judicial days following the filing of the petition."

quotes: 55-3A-1(b): "Upon filing the petition, the court shall schedule a hearing, which may not be less than five nor more than 10 judicial days following the filing of the petition."
55-3A-3(f): "The court order shall specify the time when the tenant shall vacate the property, taking into consideration such factors as the nature of the property..."
55-3A-3(g): "During the pendency of any such appeal, the tenant is not entitled to remain in possession of the property if the period of the tenancy has otherwise expired."
hearingStaySources.note: Hearing window counted in judicial days from filing. No fixed statutory stay: the court sets the vacate date case by case, and an appeal (20 days, 50-5-12(a)) does not keep the tenant in possession. The file's 10-day stay is not supported by these sections.

US-WY.note: Recalled, not read; 3-day notice to quit.
US-WY.verificationFailed: wyoleg.gov statutes site is a JavaScript app; Justia 403.

quotes: 1-21-1004: "Such service shall be not less than three (3) nor more than twelve (12) days before the day of trial set by the judge."
1-21-1012: "...the court shall, at the request of the plaintiff, his agent or attorney, issue a writ of restitution thereon."
1-21-1013: "Unless the defendant takes an appeal, the officer shall execute the writ of restitution within two (2) days after receiving it, Sundays excepted"
hearingStaySources.note: No statutory waiting period before the writ; the 2-day figure is an outer limit for the officer to execute it. No written answer required.
